stage_notes:
Scored the four hypotheses carrying both a stage 3 pass and a stage 4 pass: H-001, H-002, H-009, H-011. The eleven rejects are carried forward untouched and receive no novelty block and no rank. Ranking is by composite = 0.4*literature_gap + 0.35*mechanism + 0.25*feasibility, computed per hypothesis and shown in each scoring_note.

HOW I RESOLVED THE MISSING `verified` FLAGS. No prior_negative_evidence entry in this set carries a `verified` field; every entry was summarised by stage 1/2 rather than marked as retrieved and read. The schema says an unverified entry must not be treated as established, so I did not treat any of them as settled fact. My uniform rule: an unflagged entry discounts the literature gap by roughly half of what the same entry would discount if verified, and I raise that discount back toward full weight only where the entry is independently corroborated by a claim already in the graph (which makes fabrication or misreading unlikely), or where several independent unflagged entries converge on the same conclusion. Applied concretely: H-001's three entries converge (a formal interaction null at n=2276, a randomized-comparator meta-analysis, and a published paper whose title is the hypothesis) so they discount heavily even unverified; H-002's De Giglio entry is corroborated by graph claim C-026 so it discounts near full weight; H-009's Ricciuti entry is corroborated by C-015/C-016 so likewise; H-011's only undercutting entry is an eight-year-old conference abstract that never became a paper, which is weak coverage even before the verification discount, so it barely moves the score. Each note states the direction I resolved it.

WHAT I WOULD ACTUALLY PRE-REGISTER. Two of the four, and rank order is not a recommendation to test everything.

Pre-register: H-011. It is the only one of the four where a genuinely unasked question meets a design that can answer it. The formal TMB-by-STK11 interaction has never been estimated with a confidence interval; the one prior entry claiming the direction is a 2018 conference abstract about the STK11/KEAP1 pair, not STK11 alone, and KEYNOTE-042 with 33 mutant patients was structurally incapable of the test. Stage 4 makes it the best-powered survivor (~1.25 ratio of per-SD hazard ratios, continuous specification, ~2140 patients), and both exposure and modifier are variant calls rather than NLP. Its costs are real but bounded: TMB comparability across panel versions rests on an assumption the schema cannot verify, and the ICI-only design means the claimed ICI-specificity is asserted rather than shown.

Pre-register: H-001, with a stated reservation. It scores second on the strength of its mechanism, not its gap — it is the only hypothesis here whose causal chain discriminates prognostic from predictive and whose estimand is exactly that discrimination, because it is the only one with a non-ICI arm. But its literature gap is thin (1.5): Papillon-Cavanagh already ran this interaction at n=2276 and found null, a randomized-comparator meta-analysis agrees, and the prognostic reading is already in print under a title that states it. The increment on offer is narrowing 0.76-1.67 to roughly 0.72-1.40 in a chemo-immunotherapy era Papillon-Cavanagh predates. That is a worthwhile era-updating replication, not a new question. And the reservation is specific: PD-L1 is absent from the cohort and is an uncontrolled confounder of first-line regimen choice, which is precisely the axis the interaction is estimated on. If the slot budget is one, spend it on H-011.

Ranked but I would not spend a slot: H-009 and H-002.

H-009 (rank 3) is a good mechanism attached to a test that is designed to be inconclusive. Stage 4 puts the minimum detectable ratio-of-hazard-ratios at ~1.70 against a literature-implied target of 1.6-2.0, so the target straddles the detection threshold, and the prereg would have to declare in advance that a null below 1.7 must not be read as evidence against the interaction. The single cell the estimate rests on (~86 KRAS-wildtype/STK11-mutant) contributes over half the interaction variance and is also the cell most depleted by STK11 panel callability. Meanwhile the stratified pattern is already published twice, at n=1261 and in a second independent abstract. Paying a slot to buy a formal confidence interval that will most likely be too wide to separate the hypotheses is not a good trade.

H-002 (rank 4) has the strongest gap of the two I am declining — two small cohorts performed the mutual adjustment and reached opposite orderings, and nobody has done it at scale. But its measurement structure works directly against its estimand. Stage 4 flags missing-not-at-random co-mutation ascertainment as acute here more than for any other survivor: the estimand is a comparison BETWEEN two genes whose panel coverage histories differ, so differential callability biases the answer toward STK11 by construction, and the analysable denominator after restricting to panels calling both genes is unknown and could be materially smaller than the derivation assumes. On top of that the hypothesis as literally worded is not a testable contrast — non-collapsibility guarantees the predicted STK11 attenuation with zero causal contribution from KEAP1 — so stage 4 had to respecify the primary estimand to the single-mutant contrast, and the two identifying cells are the two smallest in the design. A hypothesis whose stated claim had to be replaced to become testable, and whose replacement sits at ~1.57 against a ~1.9 target that may shrink once the denominator is counted, should not consume a pre-registration.

One pipeline-level reason to keep the set small: R6 applies Benjamini-Hochberg across the full pre-registered batch, so every marginal hypothesis added costs the well-powered ones their significance threshold. Two slots on H-011 and H-001 is a better batch than four.

novelty.scoring_note:
Arithmetic: 0.4*1.5 = 0.600; 0.35*4.8 = 1.680; 0.25*2.5 = 0.625; composite = 0.600 + 1.680 + 0.625 = 2.905.

LITERATURE GAP 1.5. The gap_type is 'contradiction' but the prior_negative_evidence undercuts it, and I scored it against itself rather than against the label. Papillon-Cavanagh (n=2276) did not merely study STK11 - it ran this exact interaction and reported it null on both PFS (1.05, 0.76-1.44) and OS (1.13, 0.76-1.67). The ASCO 2025 meta-analysis supplies a randomized-comparator null for the predictive reading. PMID 34500370 puts the prognostic interpretation in print under a title that is essentially this hypothesis as a question. The origin is candid about this: 'the novelty here is the formal interaction estimate at modern scale, not the idea.' That is the definition of a rubric 1 - largely answered, this is a replication - and I did not rescue it. I scored 1.5 rather than 1.0 for one specific and defensible increment: Papillon-Cavanagh is a 2020 non-squamous-only cohort predating chemo-immunotherapy as first-line standard, so an era-updated estimate is not the same estimate. VERIFICATION HANDLING: none of the three entries carries `verified`, so I treated none as established. But all three are unflagged and all three point the same way, and convergence across three independent summaries is harder to explain by summarisation error than a single entry would be. I therefore resolved the ambiguity AGAINST the hypothesis - the discount stands close to what verified entries would earn - rather than crediting the hypothesis with a gap that three separate sources say is filled. Had I resolved it the other way the score would be perhaps 2.5, which does not change the rank.

MECHANISM 4.8. Stage 3 verdict 'strong', mapping to 4-5. Adjusted to the top of that band because this is the one hypothesis in the set whose chain predicts the SPECIFICITY rather than merely a direction: it predicts a non-null STK11 main effect in both treatment strata and a null ratio between them, which is exactly the prognostic-versus-predictive discrimination, and it is the only survivor with a non-ICI comparator arm that can deliver that discrimination. A result either way is informative. Held at 4.8 rather than 5.0 because the chain asserts the immune arm (STING silencing, immunoproteasome failure) contributes 'too little ICI-specific harm to generate a detectable interaction' without quantifying how little, so the falsification threshold is set by the power calculation rather than by the biology.

FEASIBILITY 2.5. Stage 4 verdict pass, and I do not overrule it. Credits: the primary exposure is a variant call, the strongest ascertainment in this set, not NLP. Penalties: (a) PD-L1 is absent and stage 4 names it 'the single largest residual-confounding cost of running H-001 in this cohort' precisely because it confounds first-line regimen choice, which is the axis the interaction is estimated on - a missing confounder aimed directly at the estimand; (b) indication bias, which stage 3 called the dominant threat to this exact interaction term, is only partly proxied by med_class corticosteroid and cannot be addressed; (c) the population filter stage_at_dx is nlp_extracted and ecog_ps is nlp_extracted, nullable and differentially missing by arm; (d) this is an equivalence claim whose achievable margin is 1.4, so a 'confirmed null' means bounding the interaction inside roughly 0.72-1.40, only modestly tighter than the interval it is updating. Not scored at the power floor, because 1.37-1.47 is adequate for the equivalence claim as specified; scored down for the confounding structure.

Rank 2 by composite. Ranked purely on mechanism strength; its gap is the weakest of the four.

Arithmetic: 0.4*3.5 = 1.400; 0.35*2.5 = 0.875; 0.25*1.5 = 0.375; composite = 1.400 + 0.875 + 0.375 = 2.650.

LITERATURE GAP 3.5. The strongest gap among the three non-leaders, and close to the rubric's 5 in structure: C-CAT and De Giglio are two conducted studies reaching OPPOSITE orderings of the same two genes, and no adequately powered design has settled which. What holds it to 3.5 is that adjacent work materially constrains the answer. De Giglio has already performed the mutual adjustment - the exact analysis proposed - and found STK11 surviving adjustment for KEAP1 (HR 1.97), the reverse of the prediction; this is not absence of evidence but opposing evidence. PIONeeR reports both genes null, which weakens the premise that either carries a large signal to partition. And Papillon-Cavanagh's KEAP1-by-treatment null means whichever gene wins is prognostic, so the question the answer settles is narrower than it looks. VERIFICATION HANDLING: no entry carries `verified`. I resolved the De Giglio entry close to full discounting weight despite the missing flag, because it is independently corroborated by graph claim C-026 - the summary and the claim graph agree on the same cohort, direction and adjustment set, which is unlikely if the summary were unreliable. PIONeeR is a preprint in a second-line-plus population and I discounted it more heavily on both grounds, verification and relevance. Resolving both entries generously toward the hypothesis would raise this to about 4.0 and would still leave H-002 fourth, because its deficit is mechanism and feasibility, not gap.

MECHANISM 2.5. Stage 3 verdict 'moderate', mapping to 2-3.5. Placed mid-band and NOT adjusted up, for a reason the rubric names directly: this chain does not discriminate predictive from prognostic. The design is ICI-only, stage 3 says explicitly that whichever gene wins cannot be shown to be ICI-specific, and C-014's KEAP1-by-treatment null means the prior expectation is that the winner is prognostic. So a positive result is a statement about which gene tracks a worse disease course, not about which gene predicts response to the drug. Further deduction because stage 3 flags that part of the predicted pattern - STK11 attenuating in the joint model - is guaranteed by non-collapsibility with zero causal contribution from KEAP1, so the mechanism as written predicts something the model form produces on its own.

FEASIBILITY 1.5. Stage 4 verdict pass with adequacy 'marginal but defensible'; I do not overrule the verdict, I score what it describes. This hypothesis collects three of the four penalties on my list at once. (a) It sits at the power floor: ~1.57 detectable gene-versus-gene ratio at f = 0.6 and ~1.73 at f = 0.4, against a literature target of roughly 1.9 - and the two identifying cells (STK11-only ~143, KEAP1-only ~117) are the two smallest in the design, so the estimate rests on the sparsest corners. (b) Missing-not-at-random co-mutation ascertainment, which stage 4 calls acute here more than for any other survivor: the estimand is a BETWEEN-gene comparison and the two genes entered commercial panels at different times, so differential callability maps directly onto the quantity being estimated and biases it toward STK11 by construction. (c) A derived quantity resting on a stated assumption: the analysable denominator after restricting to panels calling both genes is not computable from the schema and 'could be materially smaller than the derivation', which would inflate all three detectable effects above their already marginal values. Compounding all of this, the hypothesis as literally worded is not a testable contrast and stage 4 had to respecify the primary estimand to the single-mutant comparison. Not a 2: a study whose denominator is unknown, whose target may sit below its detection threshold once counted, and whose central bias vector points along its own estimand is worse than merely edge-of-detectable.

Rank 4 by composite. Composite 2.650 against H-009's 2.700 - a 0.05 margin, decided by arithmetic rather than by feel; no tiebreak needed, though feasibility would also have placed H-002 fourth.

Arithmetic: 0.4*2.0 = 0.800; 0.35*4.0 = 1.400; 0.25*2.0 = 0.500; composite = 0.800 + 1.400 + 0.500 = 2.700.

LITERATURE GAP 2.0. Somebody looked and reported it. Ricciuti (n=1261) published exactly the stratified pattern this hypothesis formalises - STK11 and KEAP1 worse in KRAS-mutant but not KRAS-wildtype LUAD - and an independent 2026 abstract reports the same null in the KRAS-wildtype stratum. The origin concedes the point: 'the stratified finding is therefore published; what is not published is a formal interaction test with a confidence interval'. That increment is real - two subgroup estimates are not an interaction estimate, and 'absent in KRAS-wildtype' is a nonsignificance claim in the smaller stratum - but it is a methodological upgrade to a reported finding, not an unanswered question. I declined to score this at 4-5 on the 'structurally unable to answer' clause: Ricciuti was not structurally prevented from computing the product term from its own data, it simply did not report it, which is a different and much weaker kind of gap. Scored 2.0 rather than 1.0 because the interaction estimate genuinely does not exist anywhere and because distinguishing a true null from an underpowered subgroup is the hypothesis's own stated motivation. VERIFICATION HANDLING: no entry carries `verified`. I treated the Ricciuti entry as near-fully discounting despite the missing flag, because it is corroborated by graph claims C-015, C-016 and C-017, which record the same cohort and the same stratified direction - agreement between the entry and independently mapped claims makes it unlikely to be a summarisation artefact. The 2026 abstract has no such corroboration and is a conference abstract, so I gave it roughly half weight; it is directionally supportive of the hypothesis anyway, which cuts novelty either way.

MECHANISM 4.0. Stage 3 verdict 'strong', mapping to 4-5. Placed at the bottom of that band with no upward adjustment. The chain is genuinely specific and conditional rather than additive - KRAS-driven one-carbon flux raises SAM, SAM hyperactivates DNMT1/EZH2, those silence STING - and it names its own falsifying step (if LKB1 loss raises SAM in KRAS-wildtype tumours too, the interaction is null). But no upward adjustment, because it does not discriminate predictive from prognostic: the design has no non-ICI arm, and stage 3's own confounding_risks note that a real KRAS-by-STK11 interaction may exist on chemotherapy too (C-037 shows a large STK11 effect with no ICI present), so a positive result is prognostic until a comparator arm says otherwise. The central methyltransferase step (C-030) is cell-line evidence.

FEASIBILITY 2.0. Stage 4 verdict pass, adequacy 'adequate only for a large interaction'. This is the power-floor case the rubric describes. Minimum detectable ratio-of-hazard-ratios ~1.70 at the reference f = 0.6 (~1.92 at f = 0.4) against a literature-implied target of roughly 1.6-2.0 - the target straddles the threshold, so the study is only powered for the upper half of the effect size it expects, and stage 4 requires the prereg to declare in advance that a null below 1.7 is inconclusive. The ~86-patient KRAS-wildtype/STK11-mutant cell contributes over half the interaction variance, and stage 4 notes it is also the cell most depleted by panel callability, since KRAS hotspot coverage is near-universal while STK11 coverage is not - a missing-not-at-random ascertainment penalty falling on the one cell that identifies the estimand. Panel-restricted denominator not computable from the schema. Credits that keep it at 2.0 rather than lower: both exposure and modifier are variant calls, the strongest ascertainment available, and the absence of PD-L1 is arguably neutral to positive here since adjusting for it would have been mediator adjustment.

Rank 3 by composite. The mechanism carries this score almost entirely; gap and feasibility are both weak, and they are weak in the same place - the KRAS-wildtype/STK11-mutant stratum that prior work could not populate and this cohort populates only barely.

Arithmetic: 0.4*4.0 = 1.600; 0.35*3.0 = 1.050; 0.25*3.5 = 0.875; composite = 1.600 + 1.050 + 0.875 = 3.525.

LITERATURE GAP 4.0. The strongest gap in the surviving set, and the only one whose prior_negative_evidence does not undercut it. Read the three entries against the hypothesis: the WCLC 2018 abstract reports the qualitative observation for the STK11/KEAP1 PAIR, not STK11 alone, is eight years old and never became a full paper; the Annals of Oncology piece is an editorial that reports no estimate and explicitly concludes the field is unresolved, which corroborates the gap rather than filling it; and KEYNOTE-042 assessed TMB and mutational status together but did not report the interaction and, with 33 STK11-mutant patients, could not have. That last point is the rubric's structural-inability clause operating for real - the prior randomized evidence lacks the cell sizes the question requires, not the inclination. Held at 4.0 rather than 5.0 because the direction has been asserted in print, however weakly, and the TMB/STK11/PD-L1 triad is well described, so the answer is not unconstrained. VERIFICATION HANDLING: no entry carries `verified`. Here the missing flag matters most and I resolved it in the hypothesis's favour, with reasons: the only entry that could close the gap is an unverified conference abstract that never reached full publication, so it is weak evidence that the ground is covered even before the verification discount, and the other two entries are on their face non-covering (an editorial reporting no estimate; a trial that did not run the test). Treating all three as established would still leave the formal interaction estimate missing. I would not have scored above 4.0 even with verification, so this resolution does not do load-bearing work for the rank.

MECHANISM 3.0. Stage 3 verdict 'moderate', mapping to 2-3.5. Placed in the upper half of that band, because the chain does predict specificity as well as direction - it states that TMB carries little prognostic information off checkpoint blockade, so the interaction should be ICI-specific, which is a predictive-versus-prognostic discrimination and makes the test more informative either way. Not taken to 3.5, for two reasons stage 3 and stage 4 both record: the mediating steps are preclinical (immunoproteasome compromise C-031, STING silencing C-029/C-030) and are the load-bearing links; and the design cannot cash the specificity prediction, since it is ICI-only, so ICI-specificity remains asserted rather than shown. Stage 3's alternative explanations are also live - ceiling/curvature at the top of the TMB range where STK11-mutant tumours sit, and a smoking-by-TMB effect relabelled - and both would produce the predicted flattening without the mechanism.

FEASIBILITY 3.5. The best in the set and stage 4 says so: 'this is the best-powered hypothesis in the surviving set'. Minimum detectable ratio of per-SD hazard ratios ~1.25 at f = 0.6 on the panel-restricted N of ~2140 (~1.32 at f = 0.4, ~1.21 unrestricted), against a mechanism that implies a substantially attenuated or abolished slope - the target sits well clear of the threshold, which is the opposite of H-009's situation. Both the primary exposure and the modifier are genomic rather than NLP-extracted. Penalties that keep it at 3.5 rather than 4.5: (a) the modifier tmb_mut_per_mb is a DERIVED FIELD resting on a stated assumption - the schema exposes neither panel footprint nor whether TMB was harmonised, so the hypothesis's own inclusion criterion cannot be verified, and the 70% panel-retention figure is assumed rather than counted; (b) measurement error in an effect modifier attenuates the interaction non-uniformly across strata with different TMB distributions, so part of any observed flattening is artefact; (c) TMB requires adequate tissue and is therefore missing non-randomly with respect to disease burden and biopsy site; (d) the any-line population makes left truncation harder than for the first-line hypotheses, since time origin and sequencing date can fall in either order; (e) KEAP1 joint modelling inherits H-002's panel-coverage MNAR problem. Also noted: the continuous specification must be fixed as primary in advance, since the dichotomised version is roughly a third weaker and choosing afterwards is a researcher degree of freedom.

Rank 1 by composite, and the only hypothesis here that leads on gap and feasibility simultaneously. Its weakest component is the one component a well-designed test can still be informative about.
